attrs.aria-label: Introduction

attrs.alt: Hongkang Chu

children.text: Master’s student in Computer Science, University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences
I am a master's student in Computer Science at UCAS. My work spans multimodal learning, synthetic image and video detection, and deep learning for magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy.

I collaborate with researchers at Zhejiang University on synthetic image and video detection and have worked remotely with UIUC on medical AI. Previously, I studied Computer Science and Technology at Shanghai Ocean University.

attrs.aria-label: Research interests

children.text: My first-author paper MedCaseAgent is now available on arXiv.
TRACE is available on arXiv and submitted to ICLR 2027.
ClueAegis was accepted to Findings of EMNLP 2026.
Our weighted-average CSI work was selected for an ISMRM 2026 Power Pitch Oral.
Our physics-embedded CycleGAN study is published online in Magnetic Resonance Letters.
Our NMR phase correction study is published in The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters.
My first-author work on druggable proteins was published in IJMS.

My research connects multimodal learning and media forensics with deep learning for magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy.
Deep learning reconstruction for deuterium metabolic imaging, MRSI and NMR spectroscopy, guided by anatomical and spectral priors and physics-based signal models.
Detecting AI-generated images and videos through generative-model trajectories, temporal consistency and evidence-based reasoning.
Agents and world models that reason over clinical evidence, longitudinal medical images and video.
Protein language models and PSSM features for druggable protein classification, from undergraduate research.
Research in MRI, MRSI, and deuterium metabolic imaging.
Co-developed prior-informed deep learning reconstruction for weighted-average CSI, combining anatomical and spectral information; first-author ISMRM 2026 Power Pitch Oral.
Co-authored work on physics-embedded CycleGAN reconstruction for short-readout deuterium metabolic imaging, published in Magnetic Resonance Letters.
Co-authored a phase model-driven deep learning study for NMR phase correction, published in The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters.
Collaborative research in detecting AI-generated images and videos.
Second author of TRACE, studying generative-model velocity responses and temporal consistency for synthetic video detection; submitted to ICLR 2027.
Second author of ClueAegis, using perceptual clues, forensic skill selection, and evidence-guided reasoning for synthetic image detection; accepted to Findings of EMNLP 2026.
Research in multimodal models and medical AI.
Protein language models for druggable protein classification.
Implemented ESM-2 embedding classifiers and an adapted GPT-2 sequence classifier, with additional evaluation on Pharos; first-author IJMS publication in 2024.

attrs.data-caption: Acquisition-matched deep learning reconstruction for weighted-average deuterium metabolic imaging
attrs.aria-label: Enlarge figure: Acquisition-matched deep learning reconstruction for weighted-average deuterium metabolic imaging

attrs.alt: Figure from Acquisition-matched deep learning reconstruction for weighted-average deuterium metabolic imaging

children.text: Acquisition-matched deep learning reconstruction for weighted-average deuterium metabolic imaging

DL-WA-CSI trains a reconstruction network on the weighted-average acquisition model. It uses anatomical MRI and spectral priors to improve the spatial fidelity of deuterium metabolic imaging within a fixed scan time.

attrs.data-caption: MedCaseAgent: From Multimodal Clinical Evidence to Rare Disease Case Reports
attrs.aria-label: Enlarge figure: MedCaseAgent: From Multimodal Clinical Evidence to Rare Disease Case Reports

attrs.alt: Figure from MedCaseAgent: From Multimodal Clinical Evidence to Rare Disease Case Reports

children.text: MedCaseAgent: From Multimodal Clinical Evidence to Rare Disease Case Reports

MedCaseAgent turns multimodal clinical evidence and unstructured notes into rare disease case reports through patient-level data mining, literature retrieval, and iterative tool-assisted reasoning. The work introduces MedCase-150K and MedCase-Bench, alongside a Qwen3.5-9B model post-trained for case-report generation.

attrs.data-caption: TRACE: Trajectory Representation and Consistency Estimation for AI-Generated Video Detection
attrs.aria-label: Enlarge figure: TRACE: Trajectory Representation and Consistency Estimation for AI-Generated Video Detection

attrs.alt: Figure from TRACE: Trajectory Representation and Consistency Estimation for AI-Generated Video Detection

children.text: TRACE: Trajectory Representation and Consistency Estimation for AI-Generated Video Detection

TRACE uses a pretrained Flow Matching video model to probe velocity responses in real and generated videos. It combines trajectory representations with cross-frame consistency to study detection across different video generators.

attrs.data-caption: ClueAegis: Heuristic-to-Reasoning Cognitive-skill Learning for Unified Evidence-based Synthetic Image Detection
attrs.aria-label: Enlarge figure: ClueAegis: Heuristic-to-Reasoning Cognitive-skill Learning for Unified Evidence-based Synthetic Image Detection

attrs.alt: Figure from ClueAegis: Heuristic-to-Reasoning Cognitive-skill Learning for Unified Evidence-based Synthetic Image Detection

children.text: ClueAegis: Heuristic-to-Reasoning Cognitive-skill Learning for Unified Evidence-based Synthetic Image Detection

ClueAegis connects perceptual clues with forensic skill selection and tool-assisted reasoning. The framework produces structured evidence for synthetic image detection, with a benchmark organized around forensic cognitive skills.

attrs.data-caption: Physics-embedded CycleGAN for robust metabolite mapping in short-readout deuterium metabolic imaging
attrs.aria-label: Enlarge figure: Physics-embedded CycleGAN for robust metabolite mapping in short-readout deuterium metabolic imaging

attrs.alt: Figure from Physics-embedded CycleGAN for robust metabolite mapping in short-readout deuterium metabolic imaging

children.text: Physics-embedded CycleGAN for robust metabolite mapping in short-readout deuterium metabolic imaging

This work embeds a bSSFP-DMI forward model in a CycleGAN to estimate metabolite and off-resonance maps from short-readout measurements. Unpaired training enforces signal consistency and reduces metabolite leakage in simulations and mouse experiments.

attrs.data-caption: Phase Model-Driven Deep Learning for Robust Phase Correction in High-Throughput NMR-Based Metabolomics
attrs.aria-label: Enlarge figure: Phase Model-Driven Deep Learning for Robust Phase Correction in High-Throughput NMR-Based Metabolomics

attrs.alt: Figure from Phase Model-Driven Deep Learning for Robust Phase Correction in High-Throughput NMR-Based Metabolomics

children.text: Phase Model-Driven Deep Learning for Robust Phase Correction in High-Throughput NMR-Based Metabolomics
The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters, 17(4): 1245–1253, 2026

A physically informed phase model guides a residual attention network for automated NMR phase correction. The study evaluates the method on metabolomics spectra, including brain extracts, plasma, and urine. Chuanwen Zhao is the first author.

attrs.data-caption: Deep Learning Enhanced Weighted Average CSI for High-Resolution Deuterium Metabolic Imaging
attrs.aria-label: Enlarge figure: Deep Learning Enhanced Weighted Average CSI for High-Resolution Deuterium Metabolic Imaging

attrs.alt: Figure from Deep Learning Enhanced Weighted Average CSI for High-Resolution Deuterium Metabolic Imaging

children.text: Deep Learning Enhanced Weighted Average CSI for High-Resolution Deuterium Metabolic Imaging
ISMRM 2026, Cape Town, South Africa; 11 May 2026

Weighted-average CSI acquisition is combined with deep learning that uses anatomical and spectral priors to reconstruct deuterium metabolite maps. This first-author work was selected for the ISMRM 2026 Power Pitch Oral session on AI Methods.

attrs.data-caption: Comprehensive Research on Druggable Proteins: From PSSM to Pre-Trained Language Models
attrs.aria-label: Enlarge figure: Comprehensive Research on Druggable Proteins: From PSSM to Pre-Trained Language Models

attrs.alt: Figure from Comprehensive Research on Druggable Proteins: From PSSM to Pre-Trained Language Models

children.text: Comprehensive Research on Druggable Proteins: From PSSM to Pre-Trained Language Models

This study compares PSSM features and pretrained protein language models for druggable protein classification. It evaluates ESM-2 embeddings and an adapted GPT-2 classifier, with additional validation using Pharos.
